title: Food delivery: one order
subtitle: One order from the customer's tap to the courier's drop-off, across three lanes

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.detail: Places the order in the app and later receives the food from the courier.

nodes.label: Mobile app
nodes.detail: Collects the basket and payment method, then sends the order to the platform.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.detail: Single entry point. Checks the session and rate limits, then forwards the order to the orders service.

nodes.label: Orders service
nodes.detail: Owns the order lifecycle from placed to delivered and talks to payments and the restaurant.

nodes.label: Payments service
nodes.detail: Creates the charge with the card provider and reports approved or declined back to orders.

nodes.label: Orders database
nodes.detail: Postgres. Stores every order and its state so nothing is lost if a service restarts.

nodes.label: Event queue
nodes.detail: Carries order events to the partner apps without making the orders service wait for them.

nodes.label: Card provider
nodes.detail: External payment network. It approves or declines each charge.

nodes.label: Restaurant tablet
nodes.detail: Kitchen screen. The restaurant accepts or rejects each incoming order here.

nodes.label: Courier app
nodes.detail: Shows the courier the pickup and the drop-off, and marks the order delivered.

beats.title: The customer taps place order
beats.caption: Nothing leaves the phone until the customer confirms the basket.

beats.title: The app posts the order
beats.caption: One request carries the basket, so the platform sees the whole order at once.

beats.title: The gateway routes it to orders
beats.caption: The gateway checks the session first, so only signed-in orders get through.

beats.title: Orders asks payments to charge
beats.caption: Payment runs before the restaurant hears about the order, so no unpaid food is cooked.

beats.title: Payments charges the card
beats.caption: The card provider is external, so the charge has to go out to its network.

beats.title: The card provider approves
beats.caption: The approval travels back against the arrow, so payments can confirm the charge.

beats.title: The restaurant accepts the order
beats.caption: The kitchen's accept is what starts the clock on the delivery.

beats.title: Orders publishes it as ready
beats.caption: Publishing to the queue lets the courier side react without orders waiting on it.

beats.title: The queue offers the job to a courier
beats.caption: The courier app gets the job as an event, so it can pick up and drop off on its own.

beats.title: The courier drops off the food
beats.caption: The last hop is the one the customer sees: the food arrives at the door.
